name: selection
description: File-level selection across a history of real commits: import, conftest, declaration and content-read closure over the base and head trees, global inputs, deleted files, unparseable source, selection against the history's first commit, and a graph cache that never changes an answer across configuration edits, restarts and damaged entries.

actions.init: create a fixture repository and commit it
actions.edit: rewrite one file's body, commit, then select
actions.link: add an import to one file, commit, then select
actions.unlink: remove an import from one file, commit, then select
actions.remove: delete a file, commit, then select
actions.restore: add a deleted file back without imports or declarations, commit, then select
actions.declare: add a # gv:test-dependency: comment to a test, commit, then select
actions.undeclare: remove a # gv:test-dependency: comment, commit, then select
actions.breakSyntax: make a Python file unparseable, commit, then select
actions.repair: make an unparseable file parse again, commit, then select
actions.touchGlobal: edit requirements.txt, a default global input, commit, then select
actions.toggleConfig: flip test_roots between tests and tests/sub, or add/remove data/table.json as a global input, then plan the last commit again
actions.restart: close the graph cache (it prunes on close), reopen it, then plan the last commit again
actions.corrupt: empty every stored graph's edges without updating its checksum, then plan the last commit again
actions.inspect: read the last selections without committing

mutants.name: head-edges-only
mutants.description: Plans with the head tree's edges only, so a deleted module's former importers are not selected.

mutants.name: direct-importers-only
mutants.description: Follows only files that import a changed file directly, not their importers.

mutants.name: global-inputs-ignored
mutants.description: Treats requirements.txt like any unreferenced file instead of selecting every test.

mutants.name: content-follows-imports
mutants.description: Reads a kind: content declaration as an import, so it also follows the read file's imports.

mutants.name: conftest-scope-collapsed
mutants.description: Scopes every conftest to the top test directory, so tests/sub/conftest.py reaches every test.

mutants.name: parse-errors-ignored
mutants.description: Treats an unparseable file as importing nothing instead of stopping with an error.

mutants.name: assumes-consecutive-base
mutants.description: Plans every run against the head it planned last, which is right only between neighbouring commits.

mutants.name: cache-key-omits-test-roots
mutants.description: Leaves test_roots out of the cached graph's key, so a graph built for the old roots is reused after they change.

mutants.name: parse-cache-keyed-by-path
mutants.description: Caches parsed files by path instead of content, so an edited file keeps its old imports.

mutants.name: cache-checksum-ignored
mutants.description: Trusts a stored graph without checking its checksum, so a damaged entry is used as if it were valid.

limits: One repository: three modules, a test-root helper, a root and a nested conftest, three tests, one data file and one content-kind sidecar; at most 8 operations per sampled history.

Covers import, ancestor-conftest, import-kind comment and content-kind sidecar edges, file deletion, unparseable source, the default global inputs plus one optional one, two test_roots settings, and selection against both the previous commit and the history's first commit. First-party pins, name-scoped modules, deferred strings, Django URLconf policy and plugin-registering test modules are outside the model.

The graph cache is exercised through configuration edits, restarts (close prunes the cache) and damaged graph entries. Cache misses and pruning are performance, not correctness, so only answers are compared; the analyzer-version and Python-version parts of the cache key are not varied.
Each step is a real Git commit or a re-plan of the last one, selected by affected() through one GraphCache per history; the driver's mapping of paths to file names is trusted.
